sm: This episode of Do No Harm argues that medicine has abandoned its core ethical principles in so-called gender affirmative care, meaning social affirmation, puberty blockers and cross-sex hormones for young people. The speakers say this follows from a provider-of-services model, in which the physician acts like a vending machine delivering whatever intervention the patient demands, even to adolescents and children. They acknowledge the real suffering of transgender youth and their families, but say relieving suffering must not cause harm and must rest on solid evidence. They claim the interventions were rolled out without adequate long-term safety and efficacy data, and that they can cause permanent sterilization and other changes that are hard to reverse. A detransitioner describes pelvic floor dysfunction and urinary incontinence after hormones and surgery at fourteen. The speakers say long-term and objective outcomes show no improvement, and in some cases worsening, even though patients often report satisfaction early on.

The second part compares the current situation to early twentieth century eugenics, when physicians sterilized people who were out of social favor because they wanted to be liked and to hold the latest ideas. The speakers say medical leaders today have rushed to affirm a culture that stresses identity and sexuality, driven by a wish to be socially progressive and, they claim, by money, since pediatric gender clinics create lifelong patients dependent on hormones and procedures. They say what physicians can offer instead is patience, compassion, and holistic attention to possible causes such as mental health, neurodiversity, family dynamics and trauma. They also want young people to hear that their bodies are good. A detransitioner calls herself a victim of one of the biggest medical scandals in American history and urges others to bring it to an end. Speakers predict it will be remembered alongside lobotomy and bloodletting, and they close by warning about threats to medicine's purpose of restoring health.
